text:
Marathon Petroleum bounced back 4.6% today after a brutal five-day selloff that erased 17% of its value since early November. The recovery came as oil prices steadied—US crude holding at $99.64 per barrel and refineries running at 94.5% capacity—but the stock's rebound appears modest relative to its recent losses. The deeper driver of last week's collapse was the midterm election results and subsequent political news: a Democratic Congress now favors renewable energy over fossil fuels, and Trump's comments about ending the Iran conflict "fairly soon" reduced the geopolitical risk premium that had been supporting oil prices higher.

The refining sector faces a structural headwind that today's bounce doesn't erase. With renewable energy gaining political tailwinds and Middle East tensions cooling rather than escalating, the near-term outlook for oil demand and prices has weakened—reflected in the gap between US crude ($99.64) and world prices ($107.03), signaling softer global appetite. Refiners like Marathon profit most when crude is scarce and energy demand is high; the opposite conditions are now in play.
